1.text: Paul, a prisoner of Christ Jesus, and Timothy our brother, to Philemon our dearly beloved friend and fellow worker,
1.amp: Paul, a prisoner [desmios (G1198) -- one in chains, a captive] of Christ Jesus... to Philemon our beloved [agapetos (G27)] and fellow worker [synergos (G4904)].
1.notes: Paul opens not as 'apostle' but as 'prisoner of Christ Jesus' -- the whole appeal will lean on love and shared bonds, not on apostolic command (cf. v.8-9).

2.text: and to Apphia our sister, and to Archippus our fellow soldier, and to the church that meets in your house:
2.notes: The letter is private yet not secret -- it is addressed also to the household church, so the whole community will witness how Philemon answers.

3.text: May grace and peace be yours, from God our Father and from the Lord Jesus Christ.
3.amp: Grace [charis (G5485) -- unmerited favor] to you and peace [eirene (G1515)] from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
3.notes: charis (G5485), grace, frames the whole letter: the very thing Paul asks Philemon to extend to Onesimus is the grace he himself has received.

4.text: I thank my God always, making mention of you in my prayers,
4.amp: I give thanks [eucharisteo (G2168)] to my God always, making mention [mneia (G3417) -- remembrance] of you in my prayers,

5.text: because I hear of your love and of the faith you hold toward the Lord Jesus and toward all the saints.
5.notes: Love and faith named together: faith reaching up to the Lord Jesus, love reaching out to all the saints -- the two are inseparable in Philemon, as the letter will press.

6.text: And I pray that the sharing of your faith may become effective in the full knowledge of every good thing that is in us for Christ.
6.amp: that the fellowship [koinonia (G2842) -- sharing, partnership] of your faith may become effective [energes (G1756) -- actively at work, energized] in the full knowledge [epignosis (G1922)] of every good thing that is in us for Christ.
6.notes: koinonia (G2842), 'sharing/partnership,' is the hinge word: Paul prays Philemon's faith-partnership will prove itself in action -- and in v.17 he will ask Philemon to receive Onesimus as a 'partner' (koinonos) in exactly that fellowship.

7.text: For I have found great joy and comfort in your love, because the hearts of the saints have been refreshed through you, brother.
7.amp: ...because the hearts [splanchna (G4698) -- the inward affections, lit. 'bowels,' the seat of deep feeling] of the saints have been refreshed [anapauo (G373) -- given rest, relieved] through you, brother.
7.notes: splanchna (G4698), the deep affections, returns three times in this short letter (vv.7, 12, 20) -- Philemon has refreshed the saints' hearts; now Paul asks him to refresh Paul's own.

8.text: For this reason, though in Christ I have full boldness to command you to do what is fitting,
8.amp: though I have much boldness [parrhesia (G3954) -- freedom and confidence to speak] in Christ to command [epitasso (G2004)] you to what is fitting [aneko (G433) -- what is proper, duty],

9.text: yet for love's sake I would rather appeal to you — I, Paul, now an old man, and now also a prisoner of Christ Jesus —
9.amp: yet for love's sake I rather appeal [parakaleo (G3870) -- to urge, beseech, come alongside] to you -- being such a one as Paul the aged [presbutes (G4246), an old man], and now also a prisoner of Christ Jesus.
9.notes: Paul stacks three tender pressures in place of authority: love, age, and chains. He will spend his weakness, not his rank, to win Onesimus' freedom.

10.text: I appeal to you for my son Onesimus, whom I have begotten in my chains —
10.amp: I appeal to you for my child [teknon (G5043)], whom I have begotten [gennao (G1080) -- fathered] in my bonds -- Onesimus,
10.notes: Paul withholds the name until the end of the sentence -- first 'my son,' then 'whom I fathered in chains,' and only then 'Onesimus.' The runaway slave is reframed as Paul's own spiritual child before Philemon hears who he is. The name itself means 'useful,' setting up v.11.

11.text: who once was useless to you, but now has become useful indeed — to you and to me.
11.amp: who once was useless [achrestos (G890)] to you, but now is useful [euchrestos (G2173)] to you and to me -- a play on his very name, Onesimus, 'useful one.'
11.notes: The letter's central pun: Onesimus ('useful,' from oninemi, to profit) had been a-chrestos, 'use-less'; in Christ he is now eu-chrestos, 'well-useful.' Grace turns the man into what his name always said he was. (There is also a near-echo of Christos, Christ, in chrestos -- the useless made useful in the Useful One.)

12.text: I am sending him back to you — and with him my very heart.
12.amp: whom I have sent back [anapempo (G375) -- to send up/back] to you; therefore receive him, that is, my own heart [splanchna (G4698) -- my very inward self].
12.notes: To send Onesimus back is to send back Paul's own splanchna, his heart -- so how Philemon treats the slave is how he treats Paul.

13.text: I would have been glad to keep him with me, that he might serve me in your place while I am in chains for the gospel,
13.amp: whom I was minded to keep [katecho (G2722) -- to hold back, retain] with me, that in your stead he might minister [diakoneo (G1247)] to me in the bonds of the gospel,

14.text: but I did not want to do anything without your consent, so that your goodness would not be by compulsion but of your own free will.
14.amp: but without your consent [gnome (G1106) -- mind, judgment, agreement] I would do nothing, that your good deed [agathos (G18)] should not be as by compulsion [anagke (G318)] but of your own free will [hekousion (G1595)].
14.notes: Paul will not force the outcome he could simply command. Philemon's grace, to be grace, must be freely given -- the gospel pattern, where willing love outweighs extracted duty.

15.text: Perhaps this is why he was parted from you for a little while: that you might have him back forever —
15.amp: For perhaps he was parted [chorizo (G5563) -- separated] from you for a little while [pros horan -- for an hour, a season], that you might have him back [apecho (G568) -- receive in full] for ever --
15.notes: Paul reads the runaway's flight through providence: a brief, painful separation was the road to a permanent reunion -- now no longer slave and master only, but brothers for ever.

16.text: no longer as a mere slave, but as more than a slave — a brother dearly loved, above all to me, yet how much more to you, both in the flesh and in the Lord.
16.amp: no longer as a slave [doulos (G1401)] but above a slave, a brother beloved [adelphos agapetos (G80/G27)], especially to me, but how much more to you, both in the flesh [sarx (G4561) -- in ordinary human relationship] and in the Lord.
16.notes: The hinge of the appeal: conversion has not abolished the relationship but transfigured it. 'In the flesh' Onesimus is still Philemon's servant; 'in the Lord' he is now his brother -- and the brother must reshape how the master holds the servant.

17.text: So if you count me a partner, receive him as you would receive me.
17.amp: If then you count me a partner [koinonos (G2844) -- a sharer, fellow in fellowship], receive him as myself.
17.notes: koinonos (G2844) deliberately echoes the koinonia of v.6: Paul cashes in the partnership of faith he prayed for -- 'welcome him as you would welcome me.'

18.text: And if he has wronged you in any way, or owes you anything, charge it to my account.
18.amp: If he has wronged you or owes you anything, put that to my account [ellogeo (G1677) -- reckon it to me, charge it to my ledger].
18.notes: ellogeo (G1677) is a commercial term, 'charge it to my account' -- Paul steps between the offender and the offended and assumes the debt himself, a small living picture of imputed righteousness.

19.text: I, Paul, write this with my own hand: I will repay it — not to mention that you owe me your very self besides.
19.amp: I Paul have written it with my own hand, I will repay [apotino (G661) -- pay back in full]; though I do not say to you that you owe me even your own self besides.
19.notes: Paul signs a personal promissory note, then gently overturns the whole ledger: whatever Onesimus owes, Philemon owes Paul far more -- his own conversion. The debt is real, but grace has already made it unpayable.

20.text: Yes, brother, let me have this benefit from you in the Lord; refresh my heart in Christ.
20.amp: Yes, brother, let me have joy [oninemi (G3685) -- let me profit, 'be 'Onesimus'd' by you'] of you in the Lord; refresh my heart [splanchna (G4698)] in Christ.
20.notes: A second pun on the name: oninemi, 'let me benefit from you,' is the very root of 'Onesimus.' Paul asks Philemon to make him, too, a recipient of usefulness -- and to refresh his splanchna, the heart-word from v.7.

21.text: Sure of your obedience, I am writing to you — knowing you will do even beyond what I ask.
21.amp: Having confidence [pepoithesis (G4006) -- settled assurance] in your obedience [hupakoe (G5218)] I wrote to you, knowing that you will do even beyond what I say.
21.notes: Paul never names the thing he most hopes for -- manumission, Onesimus' freedom -- but 'even more than I say' leaves the door wide open for it.

22.text: And at the same time, prepare a guest room for me, for I hope that through your prayers I will be graciously given back to you.
22.amp: But also prepare [hetoimazo (G2090)] me a lodging [xenia (G3578) -- guest room], for I hope that through your prayers I shall be granted [charizomai (G5483) -- given as a gift of grace] to you.
22.notes: A gentle accountability: Paul plans to visit and see for himself how Onesimus was received. 'Graciously given back' (charizomai) is the grace-word again -- even Paul's release he counts as a gift.

23.text: Epaphras, my fellow prisoner in Christ Jesus, sends you greetings,
23.amp: There greet you Epaphras, my fellow prisoner [synaichmalotos (G4869) -- fellow captive] in Christ Jesus,

24.text: and so do Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, and Luke, who labor here at my side.
24.amp: Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, Luke, my fellow workers [synergoi (G4904)].

25.text: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with the spirit of each of you. Amen.
25.amp: The grace [charis (G5485)] of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.
25.notes: The letter ends where it began (v.3), with grace -- the atmosphere in which a master could possibly receive a runaway slave back as a brother.
